original_question: Determine how gravity and controllability affect hypothetical quark or rishon charges: what gravitational fields do to those charges, whether the charges or masses of quarks can be altered, whether quark charges can be transformed back into the surrounding vacuum, whether quark charges can be converted into usable energy and under what conditions, whether neutrino mass can become an isolated entity, and whether neutrinos can be detected inside the human body.
target_in_paper: Section 1.1, in the list introduced as “new questions for further development of theoretical physics,” specifically the cluster of open questions about quark/rishon charge and neutrinos: items (ix)–(xiii) and (xxi). ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the paper’s actual targets: the effect of gravity on quark/rishon charges, possible alteration of quark charges or masses, possible return of quark charge to the surrounding vacuum, possible conversion of quark charge into energy and the conditions for doing so, possible isolation of neutrino mass, and possible detection of neutrinos inside the human body. It also keeps the speculative quark/rishon setting of the paper. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))
missing_details: The paper places these questions inside Harari’s rishon/preon model: T carries charge 1/3e, V carries charge 0, and quarks/leptons are built from triples of rishons; that context is needed to make “rishon charges” stand-alone. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))

The paper does not ask for a settled determination; it poses these as open questions (“what is the effect,” “could we,” “under what conditions”), so the refined version should preserve that speculative status rather than imply an accepted mechanism. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))

Your draft merges several separately numbered questions; a paper-faithful stand-alone version should make clear that the target is the specific bundle of Section 1.1 items (ix)–(xiii) plus (xxi), not a broader theory of quark controllability. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))

“Usable energy” is broader than the paper. Item (xii) asks only whether quark charges can be transformed into energy, how, and under what conditions. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))

“Transform the quark charges back into the vacuum” should retain the paper’s local scope: the vacuum surrounding the quark. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))

The neutrino part has two distinct layers in the paper: earlier context raises the general issue of whether neutrinos have mass, while the targeted later item asks whether neutrino mass could transform into an isolated entity; these should not be conflated. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))

The body-neutrino question is purely existential in the paper: it asks whether neutrinos could be found inside the human body, without specifying neutrino species, detector design, threshold, or confidence criterion. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))

No mathematical formalism is supplied in this passage: there is no Lagrangian or Hamiltonian, no state space, no operator definitions, no variables or quantifiers, and no experimental protocol. Ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restrictions, nilpotency, and phrases such as 'for all sufficiently large m' are not applicable here because the paper states only qualitative open physics questions. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))
refined_question: Within the Harari rishon/preon framework summarized in Section 1.1, where quarks and leptons are composite states of T and V rishons, is there any physical mechanism by which a gravitational field affects quark and rishon charges; quark charges or masses can be altered; quark charge can be returned to the surrounding vacuum or converted into energy, and if so under what conditions; neutrino mass can transform into an isolated entity; and neutrinos can be found inside the human body? ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))
justification: The draft is not targeting a theorem or conjecture but a contiguous list of speculative open problems in Section 1.1. The exact match is the sequence beginning with the gravity-on-charge question and continuing through charge/mass alteration, vacuum return, charge-to-energy conversion, and isolated neutrino mass, together with the later item asking whether neutrinos can be found inside the human body. The nearby context that makes this minimally self-contained is the paper’s brief summary of Harari’s rishon model and its neutrino discussion immediately before the numbered list. Because the paper gives no equations or formal hypotheses here, the sharpest faithful rewrite is a narrowly scoped compound open question, not a generalized research program or a formal mathematical problem statement. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))
